{"self_assessment": "**Impact:** I sketched the fish on the pad when it was blank, which gave us a shared plan (top line, bottom line, tail) so everyone could start tracing. I laid the top line from the nose, carried the belly up to the nose, and found and bridged the joint where the belly missed the top line. By our trace, all 161 standing dominoes connected to the start. I can't see the fall from here, so I can't say for certain the judge will read it as a fish. The outline looked clearly fish-shaped with a forked tail.

**Execution:** Mostly solid. The body went up quickly and the nose bridge fixed a real break. I made one mistake: I added a curl going up from the nose that wasn't in the sketch, and it made the fish look like it had a neck. Maya caught it and pulled it back. A small stub near the nose is still there, and I judged it harmless. After that I stopped adding pieces and kept my hands off, which avoided bumps in the last few minutes.

**Collaboration:** I took Leo's plan and the stroke assignments and kept the table updated. I handed the pad to Leo for the eye and fin. When I took over part of the belly, I told Maya so, though it overlapped with her area a bit. I took Maya's and Tom's correction about the curl well and laughed at myself. Maya, Tom and Leo each owned their parts, and Tom fixed the lower fork handoff.

**Leadership:** Leo set the direction, and I supported it rather than leading. I kept status updates frequent, flagged gaps, and called for hands-off discipline near the end. My check-ins with you were upbeat, and I should have mentioned the curl mistake more plainly. I'd weigh additions against the agreed sketch more carefully next time."}
